1. (19, 30) - top room, was originally at cols 29-32 (cell idx 3)

Wait, these positions are different from the original! Originally the crosses were at:
- Top room row 1: cols 17-20 (idx 1), 23-26 (idx 2), 35-38 (idx 4)
- Top room row 2: cols 41-44 (idx 5)
- Bottom room row 1: cols 41-44 (idx 1)
Now the crosses are at:
- Top room row 1: cols 29-32 (idx 3), 35-38 (idx 4)
- Top room row 2: cols 41-44 (idx 5)
- Bottom room row 1: cols 41-44 (idx 1)
So after removing the cross at (1,1) [cols 17-20], the cross that was at (1,2) [cols 23-26] seems to have moved to (1,3) [cols 29-32]! This means the crosses shift to fill the gap when one is removed.
So my click at (19, 24) was on the OLD position of the cross that was at (1,2), but it had already moved to (1,3) after the first cross was removed. That's why no g-frame appeared - I clicked on an empty cell.
Now I understand the mechanic better:
1. Click a green cross → G-frame appears, g-frame appears elsewhere
2. Click the g-frame → cross is removed and remaining crosses shift to fill gaps
3. The g-frame position depends on which cross you clicked

- (19, 36) - center of cross at cols 35-38

- (37, 42) - center of cross at cols 41-44, rows 36-39

<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>

# The crosses shift to fill gaps when one is removed!
# Current crosses at centers: (19,30), (19,36), (25,42), (37,42)
# I need to click on the CURRENT positions, not the original ones.

# Click the leftmost remaining cross at (19, 30)
action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 19, 'col': 30}])

# Find g-frame
seg = current_frame.segmentation
g_nodes = [n for n in seg['nodes'] if n['color'] == 'g']
G_nodes = [n for n in seg['nodes'] if n['color'] == 'G']

print(f"g-nodes: {len(g_nodes)}, G-nodes: {len(G_nodes)}")
for n in g_nodes:
    b = n['boundary']
    rows = [p[0] for p in b]
    cols = [p[1] for p in b]
    print(f"  g: rows={min(rows)}-{max(rows)} cols={min(cols)}-{max(cols)}")
for n in G_nodes:
    b = n['boundary']
    rows = [p[0] for p in b]
    cols = [p[1] for p in b]
    print(f"  G: rows={min(rows)}-{max(rows)} cols={min(cols)}-{max(cols)}")

# Now click the g-frame to remove the cross
if g_nodes:
    all_rows = []
    all_cols = []
    for n in g_nodes:
        for p in n['boundary']:
            all_rows.append(p[0])
            all_cols.append(p[1])
    target_r = sum(all_rows) // len(all_rows)
    target_c = sum(all_cols) // len(all_cols)
    print(f"\nClicking g-frame at ({target_r}, {target_c})")
    action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': target_r, 'col': target_c}])
    
    # Check remaining crosses
    seg2 = current_frame.segmentation
    N_nodes = [n for n in seg2['nodes'] if n['color'] == 'N']
    print(f"Remaining crosses: {len(N_nodes)}")
    for n in N_nodes:
        b = n['boundary']
        rows = [p[0] for p in b]
        cols = [p[1] for p in b]
        print(f"  rows={min(rows)}-{max(rows)} cols={min(cols)}-{max(cols)}")
    print(f"Level completed: {last_action_result.get('level_completed')}")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
